# Paths only a repo ADMIN may change. One extended-regex per line, matched against
# repo-relative paths. Blank lines and #-comments ignored.
#
# SINGLE SOURCE for the boundary. Read by:
#   .github/workflows/validate.yml       (fails a non-admin PR that touches these)
#   scripts/start_review_session.sh      (warns before you commit)
# .github/CODEOWNERS must be kept in step by hand — it is GitHub's own format and cannot
# read this file. scripts/check_admin_paths.py asserts the two agree, and CI runs it.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE RULE
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Contributors MAY change knowledge content inside a Knowledge-<Domain>/ folder — the
# Conf-, Docusaurus-, FAQ-, Misc-, Training- and GitHub- files. That is the point of having
# contributors: they know the subject matter.
#
# Only admins may change anything that decides WHICH AGENT answers, or how the repo itself
# operates. Getting routing wrong misroutes every conversation, not just one answer, and the
# damage is invisible in the transcript that caused it.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Team-level routing
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The team routing layer: which sub-agent gets the question.
^README\.md$
# The router's actual prompt, plus config backups that are the only copy of a live object.
^team-config/
# _START_HERE.md is NOT admin-only. It belongs to whoever owns the corpus it sits in.
#
# It used to be listed here, justified as "team-level routing". That justification was WRONG,
# and was verified so on 2026-08-27: the team router has no knowledge base at all
# (toolIds: [], mcpServers: [], no collections) and decides purely from its system_prompt, so
# it never reads this file. What the file actually carries is within-corpus routing plus
# SUB-AGENT hand-off advice - real, but the same kind of content as the corpus itself.
#
# Keeping it here also created a rule nobody could satisfy: CLAUDE.md tells contributors to
# update _START_HERE.md whenever they add or remove a file in a corpus, while this list denied
# them permission to do it. A contributor could not complete a compliant change.
#
# The hand-off content still deserves review - which it gets, because the corpus owner has to
# approve it, and human review is the only control that can see routing advice written inside
# a knowledge file anyway (see the note in CLAUDE.md rule 6).

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# How the repo operates
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Agent instructions. An agent that edits these then follows its own rewrite.
^CLAUDE\.md$
^contributor-initial-prompt\.md$
^contributor-update-prompt\.md$
^contributor-prompting-guide\.md$
^DAILY-WORKFLOW\.md$
^transcripts/README\.md$
^transcripts/ONBOARDING\.md$
# Tooling and the checks that gate everyone's contributions.
^scripts/
# The double-click launchers. Same class as scripts/ - they are how everyone starts the tool,
# and named without spaces because CODEOWNERS cannot escape a space in a path.
^Start-reviewing\.(command|bat)$
^templates/
^\.github/
^\.gitignore$
# Generated from GitHub team membership; hand-editing it does nothing but cause confusion.
^contributors\.json$
# Hand-maintained ownership map for review-UI highlighting. Owner maintains it.
^agent-owners\.json$
